parts.text: Which claim correctly classifies the three relationships?

options.text: Honeybee and flower: mutualism. Orchid and tree: commensalism. Worm and host: parasitism.
Honeybee and flower: parasitism. Orchid and tree: mutualism. Worm and host: commensalism.
All three are mutualism because each pair lives close together.
Orchid and tree: parasitism, because the orchid sits on the tree.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Dev studies three pairs: a honeybee visiting a flower; an orchid growing on a tree without harming it; a worm living in a host animal and harming the host.

part_answers.answer: Classify by who benefits: both (mutualism), one helped and the other unaffected (commensalism), or one helped and the other harmed (parasitism).

teacher.key_rationale: Mutualism helps both, commensalism helps one without harming the other, parasitism helps one and harms the other. Swapping labels, treating closeness as mutualism, or calling the orchid a parasite from sitting alone all miss that hinge.
